patch.value: parseMarkdownTodos is linear; strengthen linearity test to use growth exponent instead of single N-to-4N ratio

CI run 34719606517 (Node 26, job test (26)) failed: 'parseMarkdownTodos is not linear: N=5.329 ms, 4N=44.023 ms over 256 iteration(s), bound=42.632 ms (ratio 8.26x, linear would be ~4x)'. Input: '## ' + '  '.repeat(size) + '#' + '  '.repeat(size) + '!\n- [ ] item\n' at size 8000 and 32000. The test used CPU time and minimum of several rounds. Measurements (3 runs, process.cpuUsage, min of 5 rounds, 256 fixed iterations, sizes 2k/8k/32k/128k) against the BUILT parser: Run 1 — (a) whitespace k=0.9739, (b) hash-run k=0.9239, (c) letters k=0.9262. Run 2 — (a) k=0.9701, (b) k=0.9237, (c) k=0.9317. Run 3 — (a) k=0.9654, (b) k=0.9206, (c) k=0.9409. All exponents are ~1 (well below 1.2). The parser is linear. The CI flake was a constant-factor effect: the single N-to-4N ratio (bound 8x) was exceeded at 8.26x because allocating and GC-ing the 4x-larger 32k-char string inflated the 4N time under CI load, not because the algorithm is superlinear.

Step 2 branch taken: parser is linear (k ~ 0.97 for all three input shapes), so the TEST was fixed, not the parser. assertLinearGrowth now measures the growth exponent k across three sizes (N=8000, 4N=32000, 16N=128000) and fails when k > 1.5. This catches a true quadratic (k ~ 2) with a wide margin while giving linear code 0.5 of headroom against allocation/GC noise. Proven by a new test that runs assertLinearGrowth against a deliberately O(n-squared) nested-loop function and asserts it throws. The bound was not widened, no retries were added, no tests were skipped.

patch.value: Linearity test no longer flakes on a linear parser under CI load; still catches true quadratic regressions
assertLinearGrowth now uses exponent fit (k>1.5 threshold) across 3 sizes instead of single N-to-4N ratio (8x bound). Quadratic-proof test passes. 5/5 load runs pass. release:check exits 0.

Measured parseMarkdownTodos across 3 input shapes (whitespace, hash-run, letters) and 4 sizes (2k/8k/32k/128k) over 3 runs. Fitted exponents k=0.97/0.92/0.93 — all linear. The CI flake (ratio 8.26x) was a constant-factor effect, not algorithmic superlinearity. Strengthened assertLinearGrowth to measure the growth exponent across 3 sizes (N/4N/16N) and fail when k>1.5. Added a test proving the strengthened assertion catches a deliberately quadratic function. All 206 tests pass. release:check exits 0. 5 linearity test runs under parallel load all pass.

value.text: Correction after review on PR 89: the least-squares fit over the evenly log-spaced sizes 8k, 32k and 128k gave the middle timing exactly zero weight, so it was an endpoint comparison that paid for an extra measurement and was described as a three-point fit. The assertion is now an explicit N to 16N exponent, k = log(t16N / tN) / log(16), which is the same verdict with one fewer measurement. It fails closed on non-finite k, and its documentation explains why interior points add nothing and why a cliff between the endpoints still raises the 16N time. Verified: the linearity tests pass 3 of 3; replacing the comparison with true makes the quadratic proof fail; release:check exits 0.
